findings.summary: DEFAULT_PLAN_PATHS substitutes {slug} with the change_id, which for the active change is `2026-07-29-gate-authoring-space-v2`, producing `docs/plans/*2026-07-29-gate-authoring-space-v2*.md` — a pattern that matches neither of this change's own plan documents (`...-gate-authoring-space-design.md` / `-implementation.md`). The allowance then fails closed exactly where the plan claims it works, and design line 88's 'matches this repo's convention' claim holds only for changes whose file names embed the full change_id. The plan needs either a slug-normalisation rule (strip suffixes/date prefix) or an explicit instruction to add a matching pattern to .harness/plan-paths.yaml for this change.

Task 10 runs `plan ready 2026-07-29-gate-authoring-space` and Task 9 writes to `.harness/scratch/2026-07-29-gate-authoring-space/`, but the active change is `2026-07-29-gate-authoring-space-v2`; the un-suffixed id is a separate, older record already present in .harness/state.yaml, so the lifecycle close-out would drive the wrong change (stale-change hijack, pothole ④) and the live-proof scratch write would itself be blocked by the new prefix test.

`pattern.replace("{slug}", state.change_id)` feeds an unvalidated change_id straight into fnmatchcase. change_id comes from .harness/state.yaml (gitignored, fully trusted by load_state_snapshot and writable by the agent in any allow state), and `change start` slug validation does not protect that path, so a forged change_id containing `*`, `?` or `[...]` widens the pattern beyond the active change — contradicting the design's 'binds the allowance to *this* change' guarantee. Escape or re-validate the slug before substitution.

Task 5 calls `load_plan_paths(root)` unconditionally at both gate construction sites, adding a YAML read+parse to every pre-tool-use hook invocation even though the patterns are only consulted in INTENT_DECLARED; on a hot path this project has otherwise optimised (import-light decisions module, daemon demoted for cold-start cost) the load should be deferred behind the state check or made lazy.

The design designates `.harness/plan-paths.yaml` as tracked config whose edits are themselves gated, and Task 6 ships the skeleton for new repos, but no task creates/commits it in this repo and it is absent from the Task 10 `--scope` list — if the implementer does add it (which GAS-001 effectively forces), the merge gate will reject the change for an out-of-scope file.

checklist.note: The delta's new coverage section marks OpenSpec 'fully' covered and routes only the superpowers residue to docs/limitations.md, but the shipped skeleton comments the openspec pattern out — so the design's stated motivation (both adapters' automatic plan_ready path is dead under the hot-path gate) remains undelivered by default for BOTH framework adapters, and only one half of that is recorded. See F1.

Both substantive code changes check out. glob.escape correctly neutralises *, ? and [...] in a forged change_id while the added positive test confirms a literal metachar slug still matches its own file under fnmatchcase. The deferred load cannot diverge from the gate: hook_entry._decide passes snapshot.state into decide(), which gates on the same PLAN_PATH_ALLOW_STATES, and cli/gate.py:159-160 has an equivalent snapshot in scope. isinstance(change_id, str) is a correct addition given the PyYAML-typed-scalar pothole this repo has already been bitten by.

Task 10's --scope correctly gains .harness/plan-paths.yaml and the renamed plan documents, matching the change record already in .harness/state.yaml. One residual hazard around the rename's deleted paths is filed as F4 rather than a fail, since whether it bites depends on git rename detection at attest time.

findings.summary: The new per-adapter coverage table marks OpenSpec 'fully' covered, but Task 6's skeleton ships the openspec pattern commented out and init's --framework is a documented no-op placeholder (cli/init.py:508-511, _skeleton_files() takes no framework argument). So in a fresh OpenSpec repo after this change, writing openspec/changes/<slug>/proposal.md is still BLOCK until the owner manually uncomments a line — i.e. the exact breakage the design's Why section leads with ('In any repo with the hot-path gate installed, that line is dead') is not fixed out of the box for either framework adapter. The delta is deliberately honest about the superpowers residue and routes it to docs/limitations.md, but says nothing about the openspec default-off gap, so it gets neither a limitation entry nor a task. Either record it in docs/limitations.md alongside the superpowers entry, or have `adapter install openspec|superpowers` (where framework auto-detection already happens) append the matching pattern to plan-paths.yaml.

The new test_config_is_not_read_outside_intent_declared sketch takes the `repo` fixture from tests/integration/daemon/test_hook_entry_plan_paths.py, but every other test in that module drives the gate through `_hook()`, which is subprocess.run of a child interpreter. monkeypatch on super_harness.core.plan_paths in the parent process cannot observe the child, so `calls` would be empty whether or not the deferral exists — a green test that guards nothing. The plan's own trailing comment ('drive a non-INTENT_DECLARED state through _decide') implies an in-process call; state that explicitly, and either put the test in a unit module that calls _decide directly with a chdir'd root, or assert the deferral some other observable way (e.g. a plan-paths.yaml whose read would raise).

Task 6b states 'The repo convention is <slug>-<suffix>.md (slug already carries the date)' and cites 2026-07-20-init-wizard-progressive-disclosure-design.md as evidence — but that change's slug is `init-wizard-progressive-disclosure` (confirmed at .harness/state.yaml:3165), which carries no date. The actual convention is <date>-<slug>-<suffix>.md, which is what both the design doc (line 105-109) and plan_paths.py's own DEFAULT_PLAN_PATHS comment (line 147-149) say. The prescribed rename target happens to be right anyway because this change's slug already begins with the date, but the justification contradicts two other places in the same change and would mislead anyone applying it to a normal (date-less) slug.

Task 6b renames both plan documents, but Task 10's --scope lists only the new names. A rename surfaces in the branch diff as a delete of the old path plus an add of the new one unless git's rename-detection similarity threshold is met — and these two files are being edited substantially in the same branch, so detection is not guaranteed. If the old paths appear in the merge gate's changed-file set they are absent from the declared scope, which is exactly the pothole-⑱ shape the task text invokes. Add a step to Task 6b/10 that checks the actual `git diff --name-only` output against --scope before `attest write`, and include the old paths if they show up.

Ship 'openspec/changes/{slug}/*.md' alongside a nested variant, or move to a glob-aware matcher.

The prose justifying the new helper also states facts about tests/unit/daemon/ that do not match the tree.

The delta hand-writes a third copy of a state.yaml-seeding helper when tests/unit/daemon/test_hook_entry.py (same directory) already exposes `_init_state` + the `in_workspace` fixture, and tests/integration/daemon/conftest.py exposes `write_state`. The duplicate is derived from a false premise and silently loses the env-isolation the existing fixture carries. The D5 relocation itself is correct and the deferral rationale (monkeypatch cannot cross subprocess; verdict-level assertion is vacuous) holds.
docs/plans/2026-07-29-gate-authoring-space-implementation.md is the second entry of the declared change scope; tests/ (the files the task creates) is also declared.

findings.summary: The new `_repo()` helper seeds .harness/state.yaml but never clears SUPER_HARNESS_CHANGE_ID. `_decide` reads it as a change-id override (hook_entry.py:249 `override = os.environ.get("SUPER_HARNESS_CHANGE_ID")`) and passes it to `load_state_snapshot`; when the ambient value (e.g. the real change slug) is not the fixture's `my-change`, `changes.get(cid)` misses, the snapshot degrades to state=None, PreToolUseGate ALLOWs without consulting the config, `calls` stays empty, and the `INTENT_DECLARED/expect_read=True` parametrization fails. The pre-existing sibling fixture in the very same directory (tests/unit/daemon/test_hook_entry.py `in_workspace`) guards this with `monkeypatch.delenv("SUPER_HARNESS_CHANGE_ID", raising=False)` — the delta reimplements the fixture and drops the guard. This repo's documented `SUPER_HARNESS_*` env-leak pothole makes it a live failure mode, and only the True case breaks, so the False cases pass vacuously and mask it.

The new justification — "Neither `tmp_repo` nor a state-writing helper exists anywhere in `tests/` today ... `tests/unit/daemon/` holds only `test_smoke.py` and `test_hook_entry.py`" — is factually wrong on both counts. `tests/unit/daemon/` contains `__init__.py`, `test_framework_observer.py`, and `test_hook_entry.py`; there is no `test_smoke.py`. And two state-writing helpers already exist: `tests/unit/daemon/test_hook_entry.py:16 _init_state(root, change_id, state, at=...)` together with the `in_workspace` fixture (chdir + env scrub), and `tests/integration/daemon/conftest.py:write_state(workspace, change_id, current_state)`. The plan therefore instructs the executor to hand-write a third copy of an existing same-directory helper on a premise that does not hold; the round-4 reviewer's erroneous file listing was copied verbatim into the plan text. The task should instead add the parametrized deferral test to the existing `tests/unit/daemon/test_hook_entry.py`, reusing `in_workspace` + `_init_state` (extending `_init_state` with `plan_artifacts` if the gate path needs it).

Step 5's commit block still stages only `src/super_harness/daemon/hook_entry.py`, `src/super_harness/cli/gate.py`, and `tests/integration/daemon/test_hook_entry_plan_paths.py`. The newly-mandated `tests/unit/daemon/test_hook_entry_decide.py` — now listed in the Files block (line 622) and in Step 4's pytest invocation (line 797) — is never added, so an executor following the task literally leaves the deferral regression test untracked and it never ships. This is the un-fixed half of prior finding PLAN-DEFERRAL-TEST-NOT-WIRED. The same block also does not restore the red-green ordering that finding flagged: the test is still introduced under Step 3 (Implement) rather than Step 1.

findings.summary: The new justification — "Neither `tmp_repo` nor a state-writing helper exists anywhere in `tests/` today ... `tests/unit/daemon/` holds only `test_smoke.py` and `test_hook_entry.py`" — is factually wrong on both counts. `tests/unit/daemon/` contains `__init__.py`, `test_framework_observer.py`, and `test_hook_entry.py`; there is no `test_smoke.py`. And two state-writing helpers already exist: `tests/unit/daemon/test_hook_entry.py:16 _init_state(root, change_id, state, at=...)` together with the `in_workspace` fixture (chdir + env scrub), and `tests/integration/daemon/conftest.py:write_state(workspace, change_id, current_state)`. The plan therefore instructs the executor to hand-write a third copy of an existing same-directory helper on a premise that does not hold; the round-4 reviewer's erroneous file listing was copied verbatim into the plan text. The task should instead add the parametrized deferral test to the existing `tests/unit/daemon/test_hook_entry.py`, reusing `in_workspace` + `_init_state` (extending `_init_state` with `plan_artifacts` if the gate path needs it).

The new `_repo()` helper seeds .harness/state.yaml but never clears SUPER_HARNESS_CHANGE_ID. `_decide` reads it as a change-id override (hook_entry.py:249 `override = os.environ.get("SUPER_HARNESS_CHANGE_ID")`) and passes it to `load_state_snapshot`; when the ambient value (e.g. the real change slug) is not the fixture's `my-change`, `changes.get(cid)` misses, the snapshot degrades to state=None, PreToolUseGate ALLOWs without consulting the config, `calls` stays empty, and the `INTENT_DECLARED/expect_read=True` parametrization fails. The pre-existing sibling fixture in the very same directory (tests/unit/daemon/test_hook_entry.py `in_workspace`) guards this with `monkeypatch.delenv("SUPER_HARNESS_CHANGE_ID", raising=False)` — the delta reimplements the fixture and drops the guard. This repo's documented `SUPER_HARNESS_*` env-leak pothole makes it a live failure mode, and only the True case breaks, so the False cases pass vacuously and mask it.

Step 5's commit block still stages only `src/super_harness/daemon/hook_entry.py`, `src/super_harness/cli/gate.py`, and `tests/integration/daemon/test_hook_entry_plan_paths.py`. The newly-mandated `tests/unit/daemon/test_hook_entry_decide.py` — now listed in the Files block (line 622) and in Step 4's pytest invocation (line 797) — is never added, so an executor following the task literally leaves the deferral regression test untracked and it never ships. findings.summary: The {slug} guard rail binds by substring containment, not identity: with the shipped default `docs/plans/*{slug}*.md`, a change whose slug is short or is a prefix of an older slug (e.g. `v2`, or `foo` against an existing `2026-01-01-foobar-design.md`) matches another change's tracked plan document and may overwrite it in INTENT_DECLARED. docs/concepts.md and the re-ratified d-single-gate-policy body both assert the pattern 'binds the allowance to the active change', which is stronger than what containment delivers. Contained downstream by plan ready --scope and merge-gate attestation, so it is a claim/behavior mismatch rather than an escape.

Upgrade ordering gap: the scratch allowance and the new SUGGESTIONS["INTENT_DECLARED"] text (which names `.harness/scratch/<slug>/` to the agent on every block) ship in code and take effect on package upgrade, but `.harness/scratch/` only reaches an existing adopter's .gitignore after they run `sync`. In that window an agent follows the suggestion and writes scratch files that are untracked-but-not-ignored, so `git add -A` sweeps them in — the exact failure the new comment at this line says must not happen. `sync --check` reports the drift, so it surfaces loudly rather than silently, and fresh `init` repos are unaffected.
